questions.prompt: Place YOU near the circle with Navy2 visible.
questions.explanation: The example moves YOU within the circle toward Navy2. Check Gold1 and whether the next lane stays clear; another position may work.

questions.prompt: Arrange the circle search.

options.text: Carry or pass if the lane is clear

questions.explanation: The landmark helps orient the players, but the current teammate and defender positions decide the next puck action.

questions.prompt: Gold1 moves across the circle. What should guide your choice?

options.text: The new lane to Navy2 and the net-side pressure

questions.explanation: Gold1 changed the space around the landmark. Recheck the passing lane and pressure before choosing.

questions.prompt: How can the circle help without deciding the play?
questions.explanation: The circle gives YOU and Navy2 a shared place to orient. Gold1's position and the open lane still decide whether to carry, pass, or hold.

title: Change the plan when the return lane closes
objective: Update support after a completed pass when the original return lane disappears.
briefing: Navy attacks the +x end and gold attacks the -x end. YOU passed to Navy2 near the attacking end. Navy2 now controls the puck. Gold1 has moved onto the old return lane. Navy3 waits closer to the side boards on a different angle.
cues: Navy2 received the pass.
Gold1 covers the old return lane.
Navy3 waits below.

sources.title: Hockey Canada: 7 Principles for Coaches: Puck Control
sources.use: Supports creating another option after a pass; the authored movement is conditional.

sources.title: Hockey Canada: 7 Principles for Coaches: Vision & Scanning
sources.use: Supports updating the read after pressure moves; it does not certify a return pass.

limits: The completed pass and changed lane are stated. Static art does not show timing or require a return pass. An adult may read the questions aloud.

questions.prompt: Who controls the puck now?
questions.explanation: Navy2 received the pass and now controls the puck.

questions.prompt: What shapes the new support read?

options.text: Gold1 covers the old return lane
Navy3 waits closer to the side boards
YOU must demand the old return

questions.explanation: Gold1 removed the old return and Navy3 offers another visible teammate angle. The first plan should be updated.

questions.prompt: Place YOU on Navy3's side of the ice, on a new angle to Navy2.
questions.explanation: The example moves YOU off Gold1's old covered line. Recheck the lane to Navy2 and keep enough separation from Navy3. Another clear angle may work.

questions.prompt: Arrange the closed-lane response.

options.text: Notice Gold1 on the return lane
Move to a new angle and check Navy3

questions.explanation: Find the new carrier, check Gold1 and Navy3, then offer another angle. Moving can create an option but does not promise a pass.

questions.prompt: Gold1 blocks YOUR new pass line. What could Navy2 do?

options.text: Carry or find another clear teammate

questions.explanation: If Gold1 covers YOUR new line, Navy2 can consider a carry or another clear teammate. Recheck Navy3 rather than assuming both support lanes are blocked.

questions.prompt: Why does a completed pass still need another read?
questions.explanation: Navy2 has the puck, but Gold1 moved onto the old return lane. The new carrier needs current support and pressure information before the next action.
